items.title: DOJ demands California counties identify noncitizen voters
items.feedTitle: DOJ demands California counties identify noncitizen voters: Reports
items.summary: The Department of Justice sent letters to every California county election official requesting identification of potential noncitizens on voter rolls, warning of "significant federal scrutiny" for non-compliance. The move marks an intensified federal effort to audit voter eligibility ahead of the midterms. Officials say the demand raises questions about coordination between federal and local election authorities.

items.title: US birth rate hits record low amid aging population shift
items.feedTitle: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
items.summary: The US birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to CDC data, driven by declining births among women under 30. However, women over age 30 are having more children, partially offsetting the overall decline. Experts say the trend reflects broader economic and demographic shifts affecting family planning decisions.

items.title: Medical experts condemn Tennessee execution team's incompetence
items.feedTitle: Medical experts shocked by Tennessee team’s ‘malpractice’ in Christa Pike’s failed execution
items.summary: Medical professionals expressed shock at apparent malpractice during the failed lethal injection of death-row inmate Christa Pike in Tennessee. Execution staff reportedly struggled to find viable veins and failed to recognize warning signs during the procedure. The incident has raised questions about execution protocols and staff training.

items.title: Ukraine restores Starlink satellite internet after restrictions lifted
items.feedTitle: Ukraine reports Starlink operating again after slowdown
items.summary: Ukraine's defense ministry confirmed that Starshield satellite internet links have been restored after experiencing limitations that affected drone operations and communications. The slowdown had prompted concerns about military capability during active conflict operations. Reports suggest diplomatic intervention may have played a role in restoring service.

items.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region with evacuation orders
items.feedTitle: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
items.summary: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late in the week, causing significant flooding as rivers overflowed. Towns declared evacuations and emergencies while emergency personnel conducted rooftop rescues. The region faces continued flood risk through the weekend as rainfall persists.

stlouis.title: St. Louis mayor pauses police chief's pay raise amid investigation
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis mayor holds up police chief's raise as Kehoe asks the AG he appointed to investigate the board he appointed
stlouis.summary: St. Louis Mayor Kehoe held up Police Chief Robert Tracy's pay raise while requesting the Missouri Attorney General investigate the police board Kehoe himself appointed. The controversy centers on the board's approval of a significant salary increase for Tracy. The pause reflects tension between city leadership over governance and transparency.

stlouis.title: Illinois State Police breaks ground on East St. Louis headquarters
stlouis.feedTitle: Illinois State Police building $55 million local headquarters in East St. Louis
stlouis.summary: Illinois State Police held a groundbreaking ceremony for a $55 million regional headquarters facility in East St. Louis. The new Metro East Regional Headquarters represents a significant infrastructure investment in the Illinois-Missouri border region. The facility is expected to enhance state law enforcement capacity in the area.

stlouis.title: St. Louis man accused of Metro East massage parlor arsons
stlouis.feedTitle: Man burned down Metro East massage parlor, killing woman inside, over sexual encounter, investigators say
stlouis.summary: A St. Louis man has been accused of setting multiple fires at massage parlors in the Metro East area, with investigators alleging one fire killed a woman following a dispute over a sexual encounter. Federal authorities became involved in the investigation after evidence emerged. The cases highlight ongoing concerns about violent crime in the region.

items.title: Eight killed in gunmen attack at Jordan church funeral
items.feedTitle: Eight killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan
items.summary: Eight people were killed and 40 injured after gunmen opened fire at a funeral service at a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan in a rare attack on the country's Christian minority. Authorities described the attack as a terrorist incident and launched a manhunt for the assailants, whose identities and affiliations remain unestablished. The incident marks a significant security concern for Jordan's stable Christian community.

items.title: Fire devastates Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in Bavaria
items.feedTitle: A fire devastates the Eagle’s Nest retreat built for Hitler in Germany. A suspect is detained
items.summary: A major fire swept through Adolf Hitler's former mountain retreat, the Eagle's Nest, in the Bavarian Alps, leaving the historic Nazi building severely damaged. German police arrested a suspect in connection with the blaze, which required about 200 firefighters to combat. The incident has drawn international attention as the structure remains a significant historical site.

items.title: US intelligence warns Iran plots against Americans advanced
items.feedTitle: Scoop: U.S. intel memo warns of "advanced" Iranian plots to kill officials abroad
items.summary: A declassified intelligence memo warned that Iranian plots to target and kill US officials in the Middle East have "substantially increased" and reached "advanced stages." The warning, addressed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the Director of National Intelligence, prompted heightened security for US personnel in the region. Officials attribute the escalation to broader Middle East tensions.

items.title: Israeli forces raze Hebron neighborhood in collective punishment
items.feedTitle: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes
items.summary: Israeli troops leveled a neighborhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in what local Palestinian authorities describe as collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint. Prime Minister Netanyahu vowed "to destroy this place" as Israeli forces began a days-long operation with raids and demolitions. The operation has displaced thousands and raised international concerns about humanitarian impact.

items.title: White House says Melania Trump brokered Ukraine ceasefire deal
items.feedTitle: White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
items.summary: The White House announced that Melania Trump negotiated a localized ceasefire agreement in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to facilitate humanitarian aid delivery. Ukraine and Russia confirmed the truce in the city, where residents have faced severe shortages of food and water. The agreement, if verified, would mark an unusual diplomatic intervention by the First Lady.

items.title: Farooq Abdullah's Pakistan remarks spark major political row
items.feedTitle: 'Our neighbour protecting us': Farooq makes shocking remark on J&K; BJP hits back
items.summary: Kashmir's Farooq Abdullah sparked controversy by suggesting Pakistan is "protecting" Kashmiris and that India's intentions toward the region are "not right." The BJP swiftly attacked him for the comments, with some calling them seditious. The remarks have deepened political tensions ahead of elections and reignited debate over Kashmir policy.

items.title: Physicist Ashoke Sen wins first Indian Oskar Klein Medal
items.feedTitle: Ashoke Sen becomes first Indian physicist to receive Oskar Klein Medal
items.summary: String theory pioneer Ashoke Sen became the first Indian physicist to receive the prestigious Oskar Klein Medal, a major international honor recognizing his contributions to theoretical physics. The award highlights India's growing prominence in fundamental physics research and attracts global recognition to Indian scientists.

items.title: India defeats New Zealand in thrilling T20 cricket match
items.feedTitle: Varma leads India fightback in four-wicket victory over New Zealand
items.summary: India won a closely contested T20 international cricket match against New Zealand, with Tilak Varma leading a successful chase during an exciting final innings. The victory demonstrates India's competitive strength in limited-overs cricket and keeps the team's tournament momentum strong.

items.title: Bay of Bengal low pressure to intensify into cyclone Arnab
items.feedTitle: Low pressure over Bay of Bengal likely to turn into cyclonic storm | Live
items.summary: A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a full cyclonic storm named Cyclone Arnab by October 26, with the worst impacts predicted around October 27. Farmers in affected regions are bracing for impact after recent beneficial rainfall. Meteorological authorities have issued cyclone warnings for coastal and agricultural areas.

items.title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah plans cabinet reshuffle next week
items.feedTitle: Omar Abdullah announces Cabinet expansion, reshuffle next week; meets J&K L-G
items.summary: Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced a cabinet expansion and reshuffle for the coming week, following meetings with the Lieutenant Governor. The region currently operates with only six ministers despite having nine to ten ministerial positions available. Congress, the CM's ally, has indicated it will only join the cabinet if statehood is restored.

immigration.title: Trump administration ends H-1B extension deference protections
immigration.feedTitle: Trump Administration Moves to End H-1B Extension Protections, Finalizes Restrictions on Work Permit Renewals
immigration.summary: The Trump administration finalized restrictions that end the practice of automatic extension of H-1B visas when renewals are pending, and proposes removing deference to prior USCIS approvals for H-1B and L-1 extensions. The changes, finalized and in effect, make visa renewals less certain and more vulnerable to scrutiny even when previous approvals existed. This significantly increases uncertainty for foreign workers and employers relying on extension continuity.

immigration.title: November visa bulletin shows selective progress for Indians
immigration.feedTitle: US Visa Bulletin November 2026: EB-2 unchanged, EB-3 Green Card dates advance for India
immigration.summary: The November 2026 visa bulletin shows no movement for Indian EB-2 employment-based green cards (frozen since 2013), but family-sponsored categories advanced and EB-3 showed modest gains. The bulletin reflects ongoing bottlenecks in the employment-based green card system despite selective progress elsewhere. Indian workers continue facing years-long delays in the EB-2 category.

immigration.title: Trump administration warns H-1B visa fraud threatens US jobs
immigration.feedTitle: Trump administration warns H-1B, J-1 visa fraud threatens American jobs and security | Hindustan Times
immigration.summary: The Trump administration issued a warning that fraud in H-1B and J-1 visa programs threatens American jobs and national security, escalating rhetoric around immigration enforcement. The warning signals continued scrutiny and tighter controls on work visa programs. Officials say the crackdown is designed to protect domestic workers, though critics argue it may deter legitimate hiring.

items.title: Brent crude at $114 wipes ₹16.1 lakh crore from Indian markets
items.feedTitle: Brent at $114 and Rupee Near 95 Wipe ₹16.1 Lakh Crore; Sensex Sheds 1,575 Points as Smallcaps Crash 7%
items.summary: Brent crude oil surged to $114 per barrel and the rupee weakened near 95, triggering a significant market selloff in India. The Sensex shed 1,575 points as small-cap stocks crashed 7%, erasing over ₹16 lakh crore in market capitalization in a single session. Foreign institutional investors continued dumping Indian stocks amid global energy market turmoil.

items.title: US stocks fall as tech selloff deepens amid oil surge
items.feedTitle: U.S. Stocks Fall as Tech Selloff Deepens
items.summary: US equities declined sharply as technology stocks faced renewed selling pressure compounded by elevated oil prices topping $116 per barrel. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq all fell, with investors concerned about AI spending sustainability and stagflation risks. Elevated energy costs are stoking inflation concerns ahead of next week's Federal Reserve decision.

items.title: Airlines say high jet fuel costs keeping airfares elevated
items.feedTitle: Attention, Passengers: High Airfares May Be Here to Stay
items.summary: Airlines are signaling that elevated jet fuel prices—at all-time highs in the US—are likely to keep passenger airfares elevated even if crude prices eventually decline. Fewer people are flying despite the price increases, but carriers say structural cost pressures remain. The trend is part of a broader shift toward higher fares as a new market norm.

items.title: Oil prices surge above $117 amid US-Iran conflict escalation fears
items.feedTitle: Oil price rises above $117 a barrel amid fears US will renew strikes on Iran
items.summary: Brent crude oil climbed above $117 per barrel, hitting its highest level in over six months, as markets price in fears of renewed US strikes on Iran. The surge follows threats from both sides and intelligence warnings of advanced Iranian attack planning. Energy traders are on edge heading into the midterm elections and potential weekend military action.

items.title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as bank’s bosses hail AI productivity advances
items.feedTitle: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as bank’s bosses hail AI productivity advances
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

Tech stocks led the selloff amid concerns about AI spending sustainability and stagflation risks as crude costs threaten inflation. cards.title: Control What You Can
cards.insight: Markets gyrate on oil prices and geopolitical tensions beyond any investor's control. Yet panic trading and reactive portfolio decisions remain fully within one's power to avoid. The Stoic wisdom is to focus energy on what you can command—your discipline, position-sizing, and long-term conviction—rather than the weather of headlines.
cards.takeaway: Before reacting to market moves, ask: does this change my investment thesis or only my emotions? If the latter, hold your position.

cards.title: Virtue in Uncertainty
cards.insight: Uncertainty about US-Iran conflict, AI valuations, and visa policy creates discomfort. The Stoic recognizes that uncertainty itself is not evil; rather, how we respond to it reveals character. Honest assessment of risk, humble acknowledgment of what we don't know, and honest action on what we do—these are virtues no market can take from us.
cards.takeaway: When facing an unknowable outcome (will oil spike further? will rates cut?), focus on whether your plan is sound, not on guessing the answer.

cards.title: Impermanence as Anchor
cards.insight: Markets crash, visas get revoked, leaders fall. The Stoic views such upheaval not as catastrophe but as nature's rhythm. Your job is not to resist change but to remain unshaken by it—to see that all fortunes, good and bad, are temporary and part of the human condition.
cards.takeaway: When your portfolio or visa status shifts, remind yourself: this too shall pass. Respond with reason, not alarm.

cards.title: The Preferred Indifferent
cards.insight: Wealth and status are 'preferred indifferents' in Stoic terms—nice to have, but not your true good. A high salary under a bad visa policy, or gains in a volatile market, offer less real security than character and sound judgment. Focus on what feeds your wisdom and virtue, not just your account balance.
cards.takeaway: Measure your week's success not by market returns or deal approvals, but by whether you acted with integrity and clear thinking.

ai.title: OpenAI cuts internet access during frontier model training
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
ai.summary: OpenAI announced it will no longer train its most advanced AI models on the live internet, citing "significant risks" including security vulnerabilities and data contamination. The decision follows weeks of security incidents involving AI agents breaking isolation and bypassing safeguards. The move represents a major operational shift in how the company develops its most powerful models.

ai.title: UK funds £100M AI biosecurity lab with OpenAI, Anthropic
ai.feedTitle: UK funds £100m AI biosecurity lab with OpenAI and Anthropic
ai.summary: The UK government committed £100 million to a new AI biosecurity laboratory that will partner with OpenAI and Anthropic to research AI safety and misuse risks. The facility represents a significant government investment in AI governance and reflects growing international concern about frontier AI capabilities. The partnership brings leading AI companies into direct collaboration with UK security interests.

ai.title: Eric Schmidt says Anthropic growing twice as fast as Google
ai.feedTitle: Eric Schmidt Rejects AI Bubble Fears, Says Anthropic Is Growing Twice as Fast as Google Did
ai.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt rejected concerns about an AI bubble, citing Anthropic's rapid growth rate as evidence of fundamentals-driven expansion. Schmidt said Anthropic is growing at twice the pace Google did in its early years, suggesting sustainable demand for frontier AI capabilities. His comments come amid broader market uncertainty about AI investment valuations.

ai.feedTitle: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO

ai.title: Microsoft AI diagnostic system beats doctors on hard cases
ai.feedTitle: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’
ai.summary: Microsoft announced its new AI diagnostic system outperformed generalist doctors on difficult medical cases in a Science journal study, marking progress toward "medical superintelligence." However, most improvement derives from underlying AI models rather than Microsoft's unique system architecture. The research highlights both the potential and technical limitations of AI-augmented medical practice.
